# Count outlier detection

Source URL: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
Date Scraped: 2025-12-11

---

DESeq2 relies on the negative binomial distribution to make estimates and perform statistical inference on differences. While the negative binomial is versatile in having a mean and dispersion parameter, extreme counts in individual samples might not fit well to the negative binomial. For this reason, we perform automatic detection of count outliers. We use Cookâs distance, which is a measure of how much the fitted coefficients would change if an individual sample were removed (Cook 1977). For more on the implementation of Cookâs distance see the manual page for the *results* function. Below we plot the maximum value of Cookâs distance for each row over the rank of the test statistic to justify its use as a filtering criterion.

```
W <- res$stat
maxCooks <- apply(assays(dds)[["cooks"]],1,max)
idx <- !is.na(W)
plot(rank(W[idx]), maxCooks[idx], xlab="rank of Wald statistic", 
     ylab="maximum Cook's distance per gene",
     ylim=c(0,5), cex=.4, col=rgb(0,0,0,.3))
m <- ncol(dds)
p <- 3
abline(h=qf(.99, p, m - p))
```
